hypotheses.justification: Nothing else in the statement needs it to elaborate: `ZMod p` is a `CommRing` for every `p`, so `[Algebra Rh (ZMod p)]`, `algebraMap Rh (ZMod p)` and `f.lTensor (ZMod p)` all make sense without primality. The proof never uses it either. It gets surjectivity from `ZMod.ringHom_surjective`, which in Mathlib (Data/ZMod/Basic.lean) holds for any ring hom `R →+* ZMod n` with no condition on `n`. It identifies the maximal ideal with the kernel using `hker` alone. It builds the isomorphism `e` from `Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq` and `Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective`, and the rest is a tensor-product induction plus injectivity of `eB`; none of these steps involves primality. The same proof therefore compiles with the binder deleted. In fact the assumption is redundant anyway: `hker` together with surjectivity gives `ResidueField Rh ≃ ZMod p`, so `ZMod p` is a field and `p` must be prime. That includes `p = 0`, since `ℤ` is not a field.
